# Clear and Redraw

#### Course: Canvas Foundations

## Clear and Redraw

That trail from the last page happens because old frames are never erased. Every new rectangle just paints on top of the previous one.

The fix is one line at the very start of every frame.

```html
1<!DOCTYPE html>
2<html lang="en">
3    <head>
4        <meta charset="UTF-8">
5        <title>Canvas</title>
6        <link rel="stylesheet" href="style.css">
7    </head>
8    <body>
9        <canvas id="gameCanvas" width="400" height="300">
10        </canvas>
11        <script src="script.js">
12        </script>
13    </body>
14</html>
```

```css
1*  {
2    margin: 0;
3    padding: 0;
4    box-sizing: border-box;
5}
6body  {
7    display: flex;
8    justify-content: center;
9    align-items: center;
10    height: 100vh;
11    background: #f0f0f0;
12}
13canvas  {
14    display: block;
15    border: 1px solid #ccc;
16    background: #fff;
17}
```

```javascript
1const canvas = document.getElementById("gameCanvas");
2const ctx = canvas.getContext("2d");
3let x = 0;
4function animate()  {
5    ctx.clearRect(0, 0, canvas.width, canvas.height);
6    ctx.fillRect(x, 130, 40, 40);
7    x += 2;
8    if (x > 400) x = 0;
9    requestAnimationFrame(animate);
10}
11animate();
```

Click Run Code and you will see the square sliding cleanly across the canvas. No trail. Just smooth movement.

The only change from the previous page is ctx.clearRect(0, 0, canvas.width, canvas.height) at the very top of the animation function. Now the shape slides cleanly across instead of streaking. I use canvas.width and canvas.height instead of hardcoded numbers so the clear always covers the full canvas, even if its size changes.

Always clear the full canvas at the start of every frame. Clearing a smaller region to "optimize" might seem clever, but it almost always introduces edge-case rendering bugs that are hard to diagnose. Full canvas clear is the standard pattern used in every real game loop.

![Two side-by-side canvases: one showing a trail from no clearRect, one showing clean motion with clearRect](data:application/octet-stream;base64,)

Next, you will learn how to structure the animation loop the right way so it stays clean as the game grows.
